beats.narration_text: Hola, Liam. This is Liam, in for Bear. The ask — show me what is still open on my reel: which beats still need a clip, whether the machine renders it or a human drops it in, and what to type for each one.

show.event: Cream page, serif greeting 'Hola, Liam' above the composer
The ask types itself in
Terracotta send arms — the ONE accent
Three result lines stagger in — the ask lands ANSWERED

output: --open filter → only beats still needing a clip

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea in one breath. Art todo is not a list of shots you edit by hand. It is a receipt of shots you read from the machine. Change the beat sheet, run the command, watch the receipt update.

show.event: Serif text begins typing on cream
Writer pauses; the misconception phrase carries the terracotta accent
The whole phrase is corrected — the receipt framing takes over
Final sentence holds ≥2s, ready for the body

beats.narration_text: The mental model is one arrow. On the left, beat sheet dot json — one entry per beat, with a shot block. In the middle, art todo. On the right, three files it writes: todo dot json for agents, STATUS dot markdown for you, and ToDo dot markdown for whoever owes a clip. Edit the sheet, not the receipts.

show.event: Left node lands: beat_sheet.json card
Middle node lands: ./art todo <reel>
Right stack lands: three receipt cards; the ToDo.md card is lit terracotta (the human-owed one)
Tagline settles beneath: 'Edit the sheet, not the receipts.'

props.spark: One arrow. Sheet in, three receipts out.
props.tagline: Edit the sheet, not the receipts.

beats.narration_text: Four surfaces, three of them optional. Point it at a reel folder. Add --open for beats still empty. Add --method to filter to one lane. Add --json when an agent is on the other end. That is the whole command.

show.event: Dark terminal bar lands with '$ ./art todo <reel> [flags]'
First flag row lands: --open · only beats still needing a clip
Second flag row lands: --method <name> · filter to one lane
Third flag row lands terracotta: --json · print todo.json to stdout

flags.effect: only beats still needing a clip
filter to one lane · manim | remotion | ai-video-prompt | historical-image | user-capture
print todo.json to stdout — for agents

beats.narration_text: Here is a live run against a five-beat demo reel. Zero out of five filled. One line per beat: the id, the status, the fill method, who owes it, and the pantry slot it expects. The three human-owed rows carry the terracotta chip — they are the ones you drop clips for.

show.event: Terminal card lands with '$ ./art todo demo/example-reel'
Header line staggers: '0/5 filled → todo.json + STATUS.md + ToDo.md'
Five beat rows stagger in — B00 to B04, methods laid out left-to-right
The three human-owed rows (B02/B03/B04) hold the terracotta chip; the two pipeline rows stay muted

props.spark: Live receipt. Five beats, zero filled.

beats.narration_text: Under the hood, each beat is one small dictionary. Status is filled or needs-fill, decided by what is on disk. Method and who come from the beat's shot block. Slot is the filename the pantry expects. Prompt and label are seeds — they teach whoever fills it what the beat is for.

show.event: White card lands on cream with a JSON-shaped entry
Six field rows stagger, terracotta indicator bar walks down each key as narration names it
The slot filename is highlighted (the pantry contract)
The prompt + label rows hold, marked as seeds

props.spark: One entry. Six fields. Nothing invented.

beats.narration_text: Five ways a beat gets filled, and the sheet decides which. Remotion and Manim are the pipeline lanes — the machine renders them. Historical image and user capture are on you. Ai-video-prompt is the fallback when nothing is annotated — the ledger drops a search seed so you are not staring at a blank. Two lanes render themselves. Three lanes wait for the human.

show.event: Table header lands: method · owner · how the sheet says it
Row 1: remotion · PIPELINE · shot.remotion.pattern
Row 2: manim · PIPELINE · shot.manim / engine=manim
Row 3: historical-image · HUMAN · shot.source=archive
Row 4: user-capture · HUMAN · shot.source=screen
Row 5: ai-video-prompt · HUMAN · no annotation → suggest a clip

props.spark: Five lanes. The sheet decides. Two are on the machine.

beats.narration_text: This is why the ledger exists. Add --method manim --open and it prints only the manim beats that are still empty. An agent walks that list, renders each one, drops the mp4 at the named slot, and re-runs the command. When a beat is filled, it drops off the list on its own. The ledger is the queue.

show.event: Command bar lands with the --method manim --open filter lit terracotta
QUEUE card lands: B01 · manim/B01.mp4
RENDER + DROP card lands: render_manim → save at slot
RE-RUN card lands: same command, refreshed receipt
QUEUE card lands empty with a terracotta 'filled — drops off' caption

props.spark: An agent walks the filter. When a beat fills, it drops off.

beats.narration_text: One failure worth knowing. Point it at a folder that has no beat sheet, and it stops on the first line — no ledger, exit code one. The recovery is not a flag. Author the sheet, or point the command at the folder that actually has one. The ledger refuses to guess. That refusal is the feature.

show.event: Terminal card lands: '$ ./art todo demo/empty-reel'
Red-tinted stderr line lands: '[todo] no beat_sheet.json in .../empty-reel'
Terracotta 'exit 1 · refused' chip lands
Recovery card lands beneath: author the sheet, or point at a folder that has one

props.spark: Refuses loud. No sheet, no ledger.

beats.narration_text: So — art todo. A derived receipt of the beat sheet. Three outputs from one read. Five fill lanes, two of them the pipeline handles for you. A method-and-open filter that turns the ledger into an agent's work queue. And it fails loud when the sheet is missing.

show.event: Claude artifact page opens
Line one lands — the derivation, not authorship
Line two lands — three outputs from one read
Line three lands — five fill lanes; two pipeline, three human
Line four lands and holds — refuses loud when the sheet is missing

artifactLines: A derived receipt of beat_sheet.json — never a hand-edited list. Change the sheet, run the command, and the receipt refreshes on its own.
One read → three outputs. todo.json is machine-readable for an agent; STATUS.md is the same table for you; ToDo.md is a fill list for whoever owes a clip.
Five fill lanes decided by shot.type × shot.source in the beat: remotion and manim render on the pipeline; historical-image, user-capture, and ai-video-prompt wait for a human.
The --method + --open filter turns the ledger into an agent's work queue — walk the list, render each one, drop the mp4 at the named slot, re-run.
Refuses loud when the sheet is missing — exit code 1, no scaffolding, no guessing. Author the sheet or point the command at a folder that has one.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code, pointed at any brutalist reel you have on disk: run art todo on this reel folder, then walk the method remotion, open list and render each one, and stop and tell me which beats still need a human. Look for whether Claude names the exact slot filenames — that is how you know it read the ledger and not the sheet.

show.event: Serif 'Your turn.' replaces the persona greeting
Prompt types itself in as the narration reads it aloud, verbatim
Terracotta send arms
Three look-for rubric lines stagger in

props.command: Run ./art todo on this reel folder, then walk the --method remotion --open list and render each one via ./art run <reel>. When only human-owed beats are left, stop and tell me which slot filenames still need media dropped in.
output: grade it: does it name the exact slot filenames (media/<BID>.mp4)?
grade it: does it stop at the human-owed beats instead of guessing?
grade it: does it reread the receipt after each render?
